correctness.rationale: For any p∈(1,∞) and independent planar u,v, uniqueness follows from strict convexity. Hölder duality constructs an exact linear rank-one nearest line map with norm R_p(w). Any closest point of a pointed planar wedge is the input, vertex, or a ray-line projection. Continuity and finite crossing of affine images along every segment prove the global max operator norm upper bound. At an interior point identity is local; for each ray a supporting dual functional strict on the other ray produces an open region where that line map is the exact cone projection, attaining its full norm. Hölder equality gives exactly axes/diagonals or p=2. Standalone verifier numerical optimization independently checked 3675 instances, 3150 pair inequalities, 210 boundary sharpness probes; numerical sampling is supplementary.

evidence: Barrios–Ferreira–Németh (2015) use Euclidean inner-product Moreau/LCP machinery and compute iterative convergence, not general non-Hilbert Lipschitz bounds.
Domokos–Marsh (2018) handle Banach-space cones in general but prove algebraic criteria instead of sharp quantitative bounds.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Dimension- and metric-general hypotheses do not dominate unless the conclusion bounds nearest-point maps sharply in the same ambient norm. The nearest full-dimensional antecedents supply characterization and algorithms, not the asserted constant. Known symmetric two-ray cone formulas imply only the restricted reflected-slope family, not arbitrary independently directed extreme rays.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The result requires combining two independently oriented active rays, a global finite-selection estimate and sharp open-region witnesses. Hyperplane norms alone do not imply which boundary pieces are globally active or that their maximum bounds the nonlinear whole map. In the opposite direction, the displayed complete cone classification strictly includes symmetric-wedge cases.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison with three original 2015 preprints and a closely matching complete 2018 author-hosted Banach-cone paper found methods, Euclidean cone algorithms, order-isotonicity and algebraic characterizations, but not the sharp global Lipschitz modulus for arbitrary two-ray non-Hilbert wedges nor its discrete ray criterion. The one-slope reflected cone is only a special family; no general prior implication established. An older equivalent formula in normed-plane approximation remains a genuine residual bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: A historical planar Minkowski approximation article under alternate terminology may contain the same formula despite targeted textual and semantic searching.
The general algebraic conic projection criteria are classical: the new contribution is their exact sharp quantitative specialization to all ℓp planar wedges, not the underlying KKT principle.

value.rationale: The exact worst-case stability of projection is a natural metric approximation invariant for conic constraints. The result completely classifies all pointed solid planar convex cones for each non-Hilbert ℓp norm, including a discrete exhaustive description of norm-one boundary orientations, beyond a one-parameter symmetric family. Global sharpness and direction-by-direction formula are relevant to perturbation robustness, not merely a substitution or finite example.
